sections.h2: Ways to sell a Temple Terrace house
sections.html:
Sellers here mostly choose among a regular listing, an investor's cash bid and a private deal with someone they know. Let two things decide: how fast the money has to arrive, and how much repair the house is asking for.

The city sits just outside Tampa in Hillsborough County, near the University of South Florida and the Hillsborough River. Little undeveloped land is left, so a house with clean title and a sensible price tends to get noticed fast.

  • Listing: reaches the most buyers, but prep, open houses and loan approval stretch the timeline.
  • Cash bid: you choose the closing date and accept a lower figure than a polished listing might bring.
  • Inherited or rented house: the deed history or the lease terms control how quickly anything can happen.

Pull together your deed, a mortgage payoff letter and the newest tax bill before requesting bids. Each buyer then works from identical paperwork.

sections.h2: Temple Terrace housing at a glance
sections.html:
The city has 27,075 residents. Owners live in just 50.4 percent of the housing units, which leaves renters as nearly half of households. Homes lived in by their owners have a median value of $334,800, while median gross rent is $1,594.

Roughly 80 percent of residents stayed put over the past year, a sign that many houses have been held a long time and carry equity. A buyer at the city's income level often needs a mortgage, so a lender's appraisal can shape a retail sale. A cash investor cares more about condition and rent potential.

sections.h2: If your house was a guest rental
sections.html:
A rental history can change how a Temple Terrace house sells, because the city runs its own program for guest stays. The rules cover a home let for stays under 30 days, more than 3 times a year.

Those homes need a Certificate of Use renewed annually and a fire department safety inspection every two years. Each also needs a local contact on call around the clock. Breaking the rules can lead to the Municipal Code Enforcement Board and a civil citation. The city's short-term rental program page has the full text.

  • Headcount limit: two per bedroom, plus two.
  • Parking: guest cars go on approved off-street spots only.
  • Quiet hours: 8 p.m. to 8 a.m. Sunday to Thursday, 10 p.m. to 8 a.m. Friday and Saturday.
  • Listings must display the limits, a state license number or Exempt, and the Certificate of Use number.

Before accepting an offer, pull the certificate, the latest inspection result and any citations. An investor who plans to keep hosting guests will ask for that file. The city's complaint line is 813-501-6769, so call it if you are unsure whether a citation is still open.

Temple Terrace has real selling points, and buyers recognize them. Riverfront parks look out on the Hillsborough River, and the city has a public library, a recreation center and a historic golf and country club. Residents are minutes from USF, Florida College, the Museum of Science and Industry and Busch Gardens.

Nearby public schools include Lewis Elementary, Riverhills Elementary, Temple Terrace Elementary, Greco Middle and King High School in Tampa. Confirm school assignment with the district before you promise a particular school to anyone.

Take a walk around your street first. Jot down how far the closest park, bus stop and school are, then add those facts to the listing text. If your house is near the river or a trail, say so. Buyers who commute or study nearby look for exactly that.

sections.h2: Closing charges for a Temple Terrace seller
sections.html:
Two charges stand out at a Temple Terrace closing: the state's documentary stamp tax on the deed and the clerk's recording fees. The tax is seventy cents per hundred dollars of sale price everywhere but Miami-Dade, and anyone who signs the deed can be held liable for it, whatever your contract says.

The Hillsborough clerk takes the tax at the moment the deed is recorded. Recording fees come from section 28.24: $5.00 for the first page, $4.00 for each page after, plus a few small extras. A draft settlement statement from your title agent, requested before you agree on a price, keeps the final numbers from catching you off guard.

  • Deed tax, due at recording.
  • Per-page clerk fees.
  • Your share of the year's property tax.

sections.h2: What happens to your property tax status
sections.html:
The county assesses your house as of each January 1 and mails notices in November. Pay early and the discount starts at 4 percent. On closing day the settlement statement divides that year's bill between seller and buyer.

Homestead protection ends once the house sells. The buyer's value is reset on the next January 1, and their bill may bear little resemblance to yours. Point buyers to the Hillsborough County Property Appraiser for their own estimate rather than copying your number.

Each situation has its own deadline. After a foreclosure judgment, the court holds a sale 20 to 35 days later and the high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit. If you want a say in who buys, you have to sell privately before that.

For a house left by someone who has died, Florida allows a shortened estate process when the non-exempt assets are $150,000 or less, or the death was more than two years back. The Department of Revenue treats a deed from a personal representative under a probated will as not taxable.

Unpaid taxes lead to a tax certificate sale, and a tax deed application can follow two years later. None of this is easy to undo, so call a Florida attorney or title agent early. A title agent can also tell you what must be paid off from your proceeds.

sections.h2: How a cash sale compares on timing
sections.html:
Without a lender in the deal, nobody orders an appraisal or underwriting review, the two steps that slow most financed closings. A clean title can mean a closing within three weeks or so. The usual order:

  1. You share the deed, payoff figure and any rental paperwork, such as the Certificate of Use.
  2. The buyer walks the house and sends an offer, often within days.
  3. A title agent hunts for liens and drafts the settlement statement.
  4. You sign the deed. The clerk records it and collects the tax.

A listing may bring a higher price, though cleaning, photos and a buyer's mortgage approval all take time. Weigh that gap against what each extra month of mortgage, taxes, insurance and upkeep costs you, and against the risk that a buyer's loan falls through late.

faqs.q: Can a Temple Terrace house close in under a month?
faqs.a: Often, if the buyer pays cash and nothing clouds the title. Two or three weeks is a fair expectation. A buyer with a mortgage waits on an appraisal and underwriting, so plan on longer.

faqs.q: Who owes the deed tax on a Temple Terrace sale?
faqs.a: Florida holds everyone who signs the deed responsible, even if the contract points at one side. The rate is seventy cents per hundred dollars of price, paid through the clerk when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: I rented my house on Airbnb. What do I hand a buyer?
faqs.a: Give the buyer your Certificate of Use, the fire inspection record and any city citations. Someone who wants to keep hosting needs that registration in good standing.

faqs.q: Does my homestead break when I list the house?
faqs.a: No, it stays until closing because it rests on the house being your permanent residence. Afterward you may carry part of your capped savings to a new Florida home, provided you claim portability within three years.
The Hillsborough County clerk of the circuit court. That office takes the tax and the per-page fees at the moment of recording.
